items.desc: obsidian-sync-mcp is an MCP server that gives AI agents access to Obsidian vaults. Prior to 0.5.7, deployments running without MCP_AUTH_TOKEN install no serverOptions.authenticate check for the HTTP /mcp endpoint, so requests are dispatched without validating the Host or Origin headers. A malicious website visited by the operator can use DNS rebinding to reach loopback, LAN, VPN, or container-published addresses, or directly issue a cross-origin request to loopback, and invoke the MCP tool surface to read, create, overwrite, delete, or move vault notes. Deployments using MCP_AUTH_TOKEN are not affected because browsers do not attach the bearer token. This issue is fixed in version 0.5.7.

Because the exporter signs both the predicate nodes and their digest list, the check proves only internal bundle consistency and allows claims with missing, invalid, or forged asserter signatures to be accepted as authentic. This issue is fixed in version 0.3.8.

items.desc: keystore-go is a Go implementation of the Java KeyStore encoder and decoder. In 2.1.0 and earlier, keystore.Decode in decoder.go does not check the error returned when reading the trailing SHA-1 integrity digest and bounds its comparison by the length of the digest actually read. If an attacker with write access removes the final 20-byte digest from a modified JKS file, the empty actual digest causes the comparison loop to execute zero times and Decode returns the parsed keystore without an error. For certificate-only stores using TrustedCertificateEntry values, this bypasses both tamper detection and password verification, allowing trusted CA certificates to be added or replaced without knowing the keystore password and potentially enabling interception or modification of TLS connections that trust the forged CA. This issue is fixed in version 3.0.0.

items.desc: DOMShell is a Chrome automation project whose MCP server exposes Unix-style tools for AI agents. Prior to 2.0.8, the DOMShell MCP server classifies the domshell_eval tool and eval command as read-tier operations that can run without --allow-write, even though eval shares the Runtime.evaluate dispatch path with the write-tier js command and has no side-effect gate. An MCP caller with tool-session access can therefore use domshell_eval to mutate DOM, window, or global state while the host approval interface, server authorization flags, denial messages, and audit records represent the operation as read-only. The bypass does not expose a capability beyond domshell_js for callers already authorized to write, but it violates the configured permission boundary for callers lacking that authorization. This issue is fixed in version 2.0.8.

items.desc: Music Assistant is an open-source media library manager that integrates streaming services with connected speakers. Prior to 2.8.0, parse_arguments() passes the caller-controlled return_type parameter for config/core/get_value, config/providers/get_value, and config/players/get_value to parse_value() and Python eval() when resolving type parameters in music_assistant/helpers/api.py. Any authenticated user, regardless of role, can reach these commands through the WebSocket /ws endpoint or the REST JSON-RPC /api endpoint, causing arbitrary Python code to run with the Music Assistant server process privileges before command-handler validation, even if the request later fails. A default installation requires no special configuration, and compromise can expose secrets and configuration, alter library data, and control the application container. This issue is fixed in version 2.8.0.

items.desc: mini-snmpd is a minimal SNMP agent implementation. Prior to 1.7, the ASN.1 BER parser in protocol.c does not verify that an attacker-controlled field length is no greater than the remaining packet size before decode_str(), decode_oid(), and decode_ptr() evaluate size - len + 1. When len exceeds size, unsigned size_t arithmetic wraps and bypasses the bounds check, allowing the decoder to read beyond the 2048-byte packet buffer. Parsing occurs before the SNMP community string is checked, so a remote unauthenticated attacker can send one crafted request to UDP port 161 to crash the process and potentially disclose adjacent heap memory. This issue is fixed in version 1.7.

MISP contains an authorization flaw in the GalaxyCluster model's captureCluster() function, which handles the import and synchronization of Galaxy Clusters. Prior to the fix, any authenticated user holding the galaxy editor role could replace an existing locked Galaxy Cluster by supplying its UUID in an import request, regardless of which organization owned the cluster. A remote unauthenticated attacker can supply an untrusted OpenPGP message containing deeply nested compressed packet structures to a downstream application using inline-detach or message inspection, bypass the intended 16-layer limit, and force continued decompression and packet processing. The resulting resource consumption can block processing threads, exhaust heap memory, and crash the consuming application. This issue is fixed in versions 1.7.8 and 2.0.4.

Prior to 0.8.1, src/trust/ChainBuilder.ts ChainBuilder.tryBuild() terminates chain construction when an attacker-controlled certificate Subject Distinguished Name equals a trusted anchor subject, without verifying cryptographic closure to the anchor public key. A remote unauthenticated attacker can supply a self-signed leaf or intermediate that reuses the trusted Subject Distinguished Name and have credentials signed by the attacker key accepted as issued by the trusted authority. The public src/trust/TrustEvaluator.ts TrustEvaluator.evaluate() path compounds the error by matching a terminus through serialNumber and falling back to anchors[0], which can attribute the forged chain to genuine trusted-authority metadata. This issue is fixed in version 0.8.1.

Client-only implementations using SharpIppClient are not affected. This issue is fixed in version 4.1.0.

A logged-in FTP client, including an anonymous or guest client where enabled, can trigger the out-of-bounds write through commands such as CWD, RETR, STOR, or LIST, causing memory corruption and a reliable service crash. items.desc: Wavelog is web-based amateur radio logging software. In 3.2.5 and earlier, the Hams of Note feature stores the administrator-supplied hon_url configuration value through application/controllers/Options.php hon_save() and application/models/Update_model.php update_hams_of_note() fetches that URL without restricting the scheme, host, loopback, link-local, or private network destinations. An administrator can cause the Wavelog server to request arbitrary HTTP or HTTPS destinations from its network position and have parsed response content rendered in the administrator interface, providing a read primitive against otherwise unreachable internal HTTP services. The HTTP status requirement prevents file scheme responses from succeeding, so this issue does not provide local file disclosure. No fixed version is available as of this review.
